blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to Maritime, Ports & Shipping. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Ports and carriers orchestrate billion-dollar physics: berth planning, crane productivity, vessel scheduling and cargo integrity. Telemetry-to-decision loops (berth windows, yard flows, maintenance) decide throughput on the same infrastructure — pure intelligence arbitrage.

items: Vessel schedules vs. Yard reality disconnected; anchorage waits cost.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Data Monetization & Analytics Products, Master Data, Governance & Cataloging, Advanced Risk & Predictive Analytics from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Berth/vessel planning, Yard/gate orchestration, Crane/equipment maintenance) on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — SOLAS/ISPS among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Logistics & Supply Chain level this capability reads as: lane-level scope 3 transport emissions with methodology lineage (CSRD-grade reporting automated). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
